lines.text: A green, mountainous island where the Kalinago held out for centuries, and where nature both shelters and strikes. This is the story of Dominica.
In 1890, the novelist Jean Rhys was born in Roseau. Her Wide Sargasso Sea would carry the Caribbean into world literature.
In 1903, land was set aside for the Kalinago, the island's first people, who had held it against Europeans for two centuries.
Eugenia Charles, born in 1919, would become the first woman to lead a Caribbean country.
Patrick John, born in 1938, would become the first prime minister of an independent Dominica.
Roosevelt Skerrit, born in 1972, would become prime minister in 2004 and lead for many years.
In 1975, Morne Trois Pitons became a national park, with volcanoes, hot springs and the Boiling Lake.
In 1978, Dominica became independent from Britain.
A year later, Hurricane David tore across the island and left most of its people homeless.
And in 2017, Hurricane Maria devastated Dominica, and Puerto Rico too, cutting power for months.
Battered by storms and ever green again, Dominica remains the nature island.
